primary_source_citation.title: US HHS CHEMM / CERT START Protocol Technical Reference: Scene Size-Up & START Mass-Casualty Triage Decision Flow

1.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Check Scene Safety first, then 30-2-Can-Do (Respirations >30, Capillary refill >2 sec, Can follow commands).
core_mechanism_bullets: 1. Scene Safety & BSI Gloves: Stop and survey for live wires, traffic, fire, or gas before touching any patient; put on nitrile gloves.
2. Walking Wounded -> GREEN (Minor): Direct everyone who can walk to move to a safe collection zone for secondary assessment.
3. Airway, Breathing (>30/min) -> RED: Open airway if not breathing; respiratory rate over 30/min or radial pulse absent marks IMMEDIATE (Red).
4. Stable Vitals -> YELLOW (Delayed): Breathing under 30/min, capillary refill under 2 seconds, and obeys simple commands marks DELAYED.
1.worked_field_example: Step 1: Read the official First Aid Requirement 1 prompt carefully and underline every action verb. Step 2: Apply the field rule of thumb (Check Scene Safety first, then 30-2-Can-Do (Respirations >30, Capillary refill >2 sec, Can follow commands).). Step 3: Verify each measurement or checkpoint against US HHS CHEMM / CERT START Protocol reference criteria and record your findings in your Scout Workbook.
1.counselor_tabletop_demo: 3-Minute Troop Tabletop Demo (Req 1): Display first_aid_start_triage_algorithm_v46_diagram.png on screen, divide Scouts into buddy pairs for a 90-second hands-on walkthrough of 'Scene Size-Up & START Mass-Casualty Triage Decision Flow', and have each pair state the key threshold (Check Scene Safety first, then 30-2-Can-Do (Respirations >30, Capillary refill >2 sec, Can follow commands).) in their own words before sign-off.
1.real_world_connection_box: US HHS CHEMM / CERT START Protocol Field Standard: Check Scene Safety first, then 30-2-Can-Do (Respirations >30, Capillary refill >2 sec, Can follow commands).

primary_source_citation.title: American Burn Association & Red Cross Technical Reference: Thermal Burn Skin Depth Classification & Immediate Cooling

2.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Cool thermal burns with clean cool (never ice-cold) running water for at least 10 to 20 minutes; never pop blisters or apply butter.
core_mechanism_bullets: Superficial (1st Degree): Epidermis: Red, dry, painful skin without blisters; cool with running tap water for 10+ minutes.
Partial-Thickness (2nd Degree): Dermis: Swollen, wet, intensely painful fluid blisters; keep blisters intact and apply loose dry sterile gauze.
Full-Thickness (3rd Degree): Subcutis: Charred, leathery, or pearly white tissue with nerve damage; call 911 and treat for shock.
Chemical & Electrical Burns (911): Brush dry powder first before 20-min water flush; electrical burns require cardiac evaluation for internal injury.

primary_source_citation.title: ACS Stop the Bleed & CoTCCC Technical Reference: Stop the Bleed: Direct Pressure, Wound Packing & Tourniquet

3.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Place a commercial windlass tourniquet 2 to 3 inches above the bleeding limb wound, never directly over an elbow or knee joint.
core_mechanism_bullets: Step 1: Call 911 & Glove Up: Activate EMS immediately and send a runner for a trauma kit and AED if patient is unresponsive.
Step 2: Firm Two-Hand Direct Pressure: Press sterile gauze firmly with both hands continuously for at least 5 minutes without peeking.
Step 3: Add Layers, Never Strip Clots: If blood soaks through the first pad, stack fresh gauze directly on top so forming fibrin clots stay intact.
Step 4: Windlass Tourniquet (Extremity): Strap 2 to 3 inches proximal to limb wound, twist rod until bright red bleeding stops, and write exact time (T=HH:MM).

primary_source_citation.title: American Heart Association (AHA) Technical Reference: Cardiac Chain of Survival: High-Quality CPR & AED Sequence

4.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Push hard and fast in the center of the chest: 100 to 120 compressions per minute (beat of Stayin Alive), 2.0 to 2.4 inches deep.
core_mechanism_bullets: Link 1: Recognize Cardiac Arrest & 911: Unresponsive patient with absent or gasping agonal breaths; call 911 on speakerphone and fetch AED.
Link 2: High-Quality Chest Compressions: 100 to 120 BPM on lower half of sternum, 2.0 to 2.4 in depth, full recoil, 30:2 rescue breath ratio.
Link 3: Rapid AED Pad Placement: Upper-right chest below collarbone and lower-left ribs; yell CLEAR before analysis and shock delivery.
Link 4: Resume Compressions Immediately: Restart chest compressions within 2 seconds after shock delivery until EMS paramedics assume care.

Full-Thickness (3rd Degree): Subcutis: Charred, leathery, or pearly white tissue with nerve damage; call 911 and treat for shock.
Chemical & Electrical Burns (911): Brush dry powder first before 20-min water flush; electrical burns require cardiac evaluation for internal injury.
14.worked_field_example: Step 1: Read the official First Aid Requirement 14 prompt carefully and underline every action verb. Step 2: Apply the field rule of thumb (Cool thermal burns with clean cool (never ice-cold) running water for at least 10 to 20 minutes; never pop blisters or apply butter.). Step 3: Verify each measurement or checkpoint against American Burn Association & Red Cross reference criteria and record your findings in your Scout Workbook.

15.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Place a commercial windlass tourniquet 2 to 3 inches above the bleeding limb wound, never directly over an elbow or knee joint.
core_mechanism_bullets: Step 1: Call 911 & Glove Up: Activate EMS immediately and send a runner for a trauma kit and AED if patient is unresponsive.
Step 2: Firm Two-Hand Direct Pressure: Press sterile gauze firmly with both hands continuously for at least 5 minutes without peeking.
Step 3: Add Layers, Never Strip Clots: If blood soaks through the first pad, stack fresh gauze directly on top so forming fibrin clots stay intact.
Step 4: Windlass Tourniquet (Extremity): Strap 2 to 3 inches proximal to limb wound, twist rod until bright red bleeding stops, and write exact time (T=HH:MM).
